headline: Fielding error in the 15th lifts Phillies past Marlins
recap: The Phillies beat the Miami Marlins 5-4 in 15 innings after Rhys Hoskins scored the winning run on a bases-loaded fielder's choice grounder by Adam Haseley that shortstop Miguel Rojas booted for an error. The inning began with Hoskins hit by a pitch and Phil Gosselin drawing a walk; Andrew Knapp's sacrifice bunt moved both runners up, and Adam Conley intentionally walked Maikel Franco to load the bases before Haseley's grounder got away from Rojas.

Starters Vince Velasquez (4 innings) and Pablo Lopez (4 1/3 innings) each allowed four runs. Miami built a 4-2 lead through three innings on Starlin Castro's RBI double, Harold Ramirez's solo homer and a two-run single by Isan Diaz, before Philadelphia tied it at 4-4 on a Bryce Harper RBI triple, a Rhys Hoskins sacrifice fly scoring Harper, an Adam Haseley RBI single and a second Harper sacrifice fly in the fifth that scored Cesar Hernandez.

Neither bullpen allowed a run over the next nine-plus innings. Ranger Suarez threw three scoreless innings, from the 13th through the 15th, to pick up the win, while Adam Conley took the loss after walking three in 1 1/3 innings.
